name: Freelance AI training specialist (Alignerr)
summary: Labelbox-run marketplace that hires freelance generalists and experts by the hour to train and evaluate AI models.
whatYouDo: You apply to a specific posting (e.g. AI Training Specialist, software engineer, language expert), pass screening, then write, review and correct AI model outputs. Postings list commitments of roughly 10–40 hours a week, some with a 15-hour minimum.
appeal: Official postings list US$15–120/hr depending on role
General AI Training Specialist posting says no prior AI or technical experience needed
Hourly contract with weekly payouts on some postings
Postings are syndicated to Canadian job boards such as Built In Ottawa
watchOuts: Published pay ranges are for US-based candidates; Canadian rates are not published
A 2026 review blog says evaluation phases are often unpaid and qualified people can wait months between projects
1099-style contract: no benefits; you must be authorized to work in your country
Canada eligibility varies by posting and was not confirmed on an official page

training.notes: Screening/evaluation before projects; a blog says these phases are often unpaid.

compensation.notes: Alignerr jobs page postings range US$15–120/hr (e.g. AI Training Specialist $40–120/hr). Ranges are stated for US-based candidates; non-US rates 'may vary'.

reliability.notes: One 2026 blog reports months-long gaps between projects for qualified workers. Anecdotal, single source.

applicationSteps: Browse open postings on the Alignerr jobs page
Apply to a role that lists Canada or remote eligibility
Wait to be placed on a project
fitsIf: You have strong writing or subject expertise and can tolerate unpaid screening and gaps between projects.
notFitIf: You need confirmed Canadian rates or quick, reliable income.
